buildLab.lede: Tap a metal dot, then tap another dot to join them with a wire. Tap a wire to remove it. Turn on the sun to test.
lab.goal.0: The panel sits above the plant. Wire the panel to the motor so the fan blows air toward the plant.
lab.goal.1: Wire the panel to the LED so it lights up next to the plant.
lab.goal.2: Run the fan and the LED at the same time. Pick a panel for each part, and keep the LED safe.
lab.goal.3: Wire a panel to the water pump so it sends water from the tank to the plant. Pick the panel with enough power.
lab.real.0: Clip the red wire from the large panel to one motor tab and the black wire to the other. Take it into direct sun. If the air blows the wrong way, swap the two clips.
lab.real.1: Clip red to the LED’s longer leg and black to the shorter leg. If it stays dark in full sun, flip the clips. On a big panel (5 V or more), put a 100–220 Ω resistor between the red wire and the long leg so the LED does not burn out.
lab.real.2: Choose the panel for each part. The fan needs the big panel to spin fast. On the big panel, put a 100–220 Ω resistor between the red wire and the LED’s long leg; on the small panel the LED is fine without one. Join each part’s black wire to the same panel’s black wire.
lab.real.3: Use the big panel in full sun: a small panel only makes the pump trickle. Put the mini pump in a cup of water and run its tube into the pot. Clip red to the pump’s red (+) wire and black to its black (−) wire. Keep the panel and clips up high and dry.
lab.status.pickSecond: Now tap the dot you want to connect to.
lab.status.start: Tap a dot to start a wire.
lab.status.turnOnSun: Turn on the sun to test your wires.
lab.status.short: Short circuit! The + and − of the panel are joined directly, so the power skips the parts. Remove that wire.
lab.status.fanOk: It works! The air blows toward the plant.
lab.status.fanBackwards: The motor still works, it just spins the other way. Swap the two wires so the air blows toward the plant.
lab.status.fanNothing: Nothing yet. The motor needs one wire from + and one wire from −.
lab.status.ledOk: It glows! Red to the long leg, black to the short leg.
lab.status.ledBackwards: Still dark. An LED only works one way: + goes to the long leg. Swap the wires.
lab.status.ledNothing: Nothing yet. The LED needs one wire from + and one from −.
lab.status.pumpOk: Water is flowing! The pump moves water from the tank to the plant while the sun shines.
lab.status.pumpNothing: Nothing yet. The pump needs one wire from + and one wire from −.
lab.status.bothOk: Both run! Each part has its own path to + and −. This is a parallel circuit.
lab.status.bothNothing: Connect both parts to the panel. Each part needs its own + and − wire.
lab.goal.5: This circuit has 2 faults. Find them and fix them so the fan, the LED and the pump all work.
lab.real.5: Real circuits break too. Check one part at a time: is each red wire on +, each black wire on −, and does the LED on the big panel have its resistor? A simple multimeter works like the Tester.
lab.status.ledBurnt: Too much power for the LED. Add a resistor between the panel and the LED's long leg.
lab.status.weak: A part is running weakly: the small panel can’t give it enough power. Try the big panel.
lab.status.panelsJoined: The two panels are wired to each other. Keep the panels apart and give each part one panel.
lab.status.fixOk: Everything works again! You found and fixed both faults.
lab.testerHint: Tap any dot to test it. The Tester does not change the wires.
lab.hint.0.0: Where does each motor tab need to go?
lab.hint.0.1: One motor tab needs a wire from +, the other a wire from −.
lab.hint.0.2: Join panel + to motor +, and panel − to motor −.
lab.hint.1.0: Does it matter which LED leg goes where?
lab.hint.1.1: An LED only works one way: + goes to the long leg.
lab.hint.1.2: Join panel + to the long leg, and panel − to the short leg.
lab.hint.2.0: Which panel is strong enough for the fan, and what keeps the LED safe?
lab.hint.2.1: The fan needs the big panel. On the big panel, the LED needs the resistor in its path.
lab.hint.2.2: Fan on the big panel; LED on the small panel. Or: big panel + to the resistor, the resistor to the LED's long leg.
lab.hint.3.0: Which panel can push water all the way to the pot?
lab.hint.3.1: The pump needs the most power. It does not need the resistor.
lab.hint.3.2: Join big panel + to pump +, and big panel − to pump −.
lab.hint.4.0: Does every part have its own path to + and −?
lab.hint.4.1: Use the big panel for the fan and the pump. Give the LED the resistor, or use the small panel for it.
lab.hint.4.2: Big panel + to fan + and pump +; big panel − to fan − and pump −; LED on the small panel.
lab.hint.5.0: Which part is not working? Start there.
lab.hint.5.1: Turn on the Tester and tap that part's dots. A + dot with no power means a wire is missing or wrong.
lab.hint.5.2: Fix one fault at a time: swap backwards wires, add the missing wire, and give the LED its resistor.
lab.part.motor.trickle: Fan: only a trickle, needs more power
lab.part.motor.tooMuch: Fan: too much power, needs a resistor
lab.part.motor.burnt: Fan: burnt out, press Replace LED
lab.part.motor.joined: Fan: off, the two panels are joined
lab.part.led.trickle: LED: only a trickle, needs more power
lab.part.led.tooMuch: LED: too much power, needs a resistor
lab.part.led.burnt: LED: burnt out, press Replace LED
lab.part.led.joined: LED: off, the two panels are joined
lab.part.pump.trickle: Pump: only a trickle, needs more power
lab.part.pump.tooMuch: Pump: too much power, needs a resistor
lab.part.pump.burnt: Pump: burnt out, press Replace LED
lab.part.pump.joined: Pump: off, the two panels are joined
lab.goal.4: Run the fan, the LED and the water pump at the same time. Each part needs its own path to + and −.
lab.real.4: Use the big panel in full sun: the pump needs the most power. Join the red wires (panel, motor, pump) and one end of a 100–220 Ω resistor; the resistor’s other end goes to the LED’s long leg. Join all the black wires plus the LED’s short leg. Or run the LED from the small panel with no resistor. Alligator clips can hold two wires each.
lab.status.allOk: All three run! Each part has its own path to + and −. This is a parallel circuit.
lab.status.allSeries: Looks like a chain (series): some parts are wired one after the other, so they cannot start. Connect each part straight to + and −.
lab.status.allBackwards: A part is wired backwards. Check the list and swap that part’s two wires.
lab.status.allSome: Some parts work. Check the list: every part needs its own + and − wire.
lab.status.allNothing: Connect all three parts to the panel. Each part needs its own + and − wire.
lab.status.cloud: Clouds mean less power. The pump needs the most, so it stops first.

home.heroLabel: A sunny sky over a solar panel on posts above a seedling in a pot, with a fan, an LED and a water tank
home.tagline: Little land. Little water. Lots of sun. You decide how to share it.
home.mission: Build a micro-lab for one sunny desert spot. Make it grow food and power a fan, a light and a pump. Then show your family how it works.
home.bigQuestion: In a desert where land, water, and shade are hard to come by, how can you use STEM to build a micro-lab that shows your family how one sunny space can grow food and power other things at once?
home.m.sunDay.goal: Run a sunny day and get your best Sun Score.
home.m.growthStory.goal: Save a photo and a few words at each step.
home.credits: Made with Girl Scouts Beyond Bars and ASU Mary Lou Fulton College for Teaching and Learning Innovation
home.estimates: The numbers are estimates for learning, not measurements.

challenge.heat.name: Challenge 1: Beat the heat
challenge.heat.goal: Heat wave week with basil. Grow at least twice as much as basil with no panel.
challenge.heat.pass: Your basil grew more than twice the no-panel basil.
challenge.heat.fail: Your basil needs more protection from the heat.
challenge.fan.name: Challenge 2: Fan all afternoon
challenge.fan.goal: Sunny day. Keep the fan spinning every hour from noon to 5 pm, and grow at least as much as a plant with no panel.
challenge.fan.pass: The fan ran all afternoon and the plant kept up.
challenge.fan.fail: The fan stopped in the afternoon, or the plant fell behind.
challenge.tank.name: Challenge 3: Water by itself all week
challenge.tank.goal: Sunny week with the pump and no hand watering. The soil may be dry for 30 hours at most.
challenge.tank.pass: The soil stayed just right all week.
challenge.tank.fail: The soil got too dry. Try slowing down how fast it dries.
rules.lowLight.why: Your {crop} got about {light}% of the sun under the panels. It wanted more light to grow fast.
rules.lowLight.next: How could you give the plant more light and still make energy?
rules.lowLight.hint.0: Light can sneak in from the sides.
rules.lowLight.hint.1: A high panel lets more side light in. A smaller panel makes less shade.
rules.lowLight.hint.2: Try the panel set high, or the small panel.
rules.hotShade.why: Leaves were above {hi} °F for {hours} sunny hours. That is too warm for {crop} to grow well.
rules.hotShade.next: What could shade the plant during the hottest hours?
rules.hotShade.hint.0: When is the sun strongest? What is above the plant then?
rules.hotShade.hint.1: A bigger panel makes more shade, and shade cools the leaves.
rules.hotShade.hint.2: Try the big panel or both panels.
rules.hotFan.why: Leaves were above {hi} °F for {hours} sunny hours. That is too warm for {crop} to grow well.
rules.hotFan.next: Your panel makes power. What could it run to cool the leaves?
rules.hotFan.hint.0: Moving air carries heat away from the leaves.
rules.hotFan.hint.1: A running fan cools the leaves by a few degrees.
rules.hotHeight.why: Leaves were above {hi} °F for {hours} sunny hours. That is too warm for {crop} to grow well.
rules.hotHeight.next: How could hot air escape from under the panel?
rules.hotHeight.hint.0: Hot air gets trapped under a low panel.
rules.hotHeight.hint.1: A high panel lets hot air out and side light in.
rules.hotPlant.why: Leaves were above {hi} °F for {hours} sunny hours. That is too warm for {crop} to grow well.
rules.hotPlant.next: Your setup already gives shade and wind. Which plant handles heat best?
rules.hotPlant.hint.0: Some plants like it hot. Read the hint under each plant.
rules.hotPlant.hint.1: Chili pepper handles heat better than lettuce or basil.
rules.hotPlant.hint.2: Try chili pepper with the same setup.
rules.hotMax.why: Leaves were above {hi} °F for {hours} sunny hours. Even chili pepper grows slowly when it is that hot.
rules.hotMax.next: This heat is tough for any plant. Did your setup still beat the plant with no panel?
rules.hotMax.hint.0: Look at the black line on the Food bar.
rules.hotMax.hint.1: Shade, a high panel and the fan each cool the leaves a little.
rules.hotMax.hint.2: Compare your score with the no-panel score above.
rules.dry.why: The soil got too dry for {dry} sunny hours. Thirsty plants stop growing.
rules.dry.next: How could the soil stay wet longer during the day?
rules.dry.hint.0: Where does the water go on a hot afternoon?
rules.dry.hint.1: Shade slows drying. The pump only runs when the panel has power left after the fan.
rules.dry.hint.2: Try both panels with the pump on and the fan off.
rules.tankEmpty.why: The tank ran dry on day {day} at {hour}:00, then the soil dried out.
rules.tankEmpty.next: How could the same water last longer?
rules.tankEmpty.hint.0: Where does the water go on a hot day?
rules.tankEmpty.hint.1: Shade slows drying, so the same water lasts longer.
rules.tankEmpty.hint.2: Try both panels with the pump on.
rules.lowEnergy.why: Your plant did well, but your panel made only {energy}% of the energy the best setup can make.
rules.lowEnergy.next: Can you make more energy and still keep the plant happy?
rules.lowEnergy.hint.0: Which panel catches the most sun?
rules.lowEnergy.hint.1: More panel area means more energy, but also more shade.
rules.noPanel.why: Your plant grew fine in full sun, but with no panel you made no energy.
rules.noPanel.next: What happens to the plant if you add a panel above it?
rules.noPanel.hint.0: Shade can help or hurt. It depends on the plant and the heat.
rules.noPanel.hint.1: Try a small panel first, then compare.
rules.noPanel.hint.2: Try the big panel set high.
rules.balanced.why: A good balance: nothing held the plant back much, and the panel made {energy}% of the best energy.
rules.balanced.next: Can you raise one score without dropping the other?
rules.balanced.hint.0: Change just one thing, then run again and compare.
rules.balanced.hint.1: Try the other panel height, or a different panel size.
rules.balanced.hint.2: Compare Big + high with Both + high.

learn.part.panel.name: Solar panel
learn.part.panel.what: A solar panel turns sunlight into electricity.
learn.part.panel.how: Light hits the panel. The light pushes tiny bits called electrons. They flow out of the + side, through the wires, and back into the − side.
learn.part.panel.try: Turn the panel to face the sun. How much power do you get?
learn.part.panel.numbers: In full sun: about {v} V and {a} A. That is {w} W. With nothing connected: about {voc} V.
learn.part.led.name: LED
learn.part.led.what: An LED is a tiny light. It uses very little power.
learn.part.led.how: Electricity can only go through an LED one way. The long leg is the + side. Wire it backwards and it stays dark.
learn.part.led.try: Light up the LED with one panel.
learn.part.led.numbers: It needs at least {v} V. It uses about {a} A.
learn.part.fan.name: Fan motor
learn.part.fan.what: The fan has a small motor inside. It spins and moves air to cool the plant.
learn.part.fan.how: Electricity makes the motor turn. More volts make it spin faster. Swap + and − and it spins the other way.
learn.part.fan.try: Turn the dial to make the fan go slow, then fast.
learn.part.fan.numbers: It starts at about {v} V. It uses about {a} A. It turns about {rpm} RPM for each volt.
learn.part.pump.name: Water pump
learn.part.pump.what: The pump moves water from the tank to the plant.
learn.part.pump.how: A motor inside the pump pushes water through a tube. The pump needs more power than the fan or the LED.
learn.part.pump.try: Find a panel strong enough to run the pump.
learn.part.pump.numbers: It needs at least {v} V and about {a} A. It moves about {ml} mL of water a minute.
learn.part.switch.name: Switch
learn.part.switch.what: A switch turns your system on and off.
learn.part.switch.how: On closes the loop, so electricity can flow. Off opens a gap in the loop, so nothing flows.
learn.part.switch.try: Turn the switch off and on. Watch the fan.
learn.part.switch.numbers: Off: 0 A flows. On: the devices get the current they need.
learn.part.pot.name: Potentiometer
learn.part.pot.what: A potentiometer is a dial. It controls how much power reaches the fan.
learn.part.pot.how: Turn the dial up and more volts reach the fan. Turn it down and fewer volts get through.
learn.part.pot.try: Dial the fan to two speeds.
learn.part.pot.numbers: At 0 %, the fan gets 0 V. At 50 %, it gets half the volts. At 100 %, it gets all of them.
learn.part.lightMeter.name: Light meter
learn.part.lightMeter.what: A light meter measures how much light there is.
learn.part.lightMeter.how: Hold it next to the panel. It shows the light in foot-candles (FC). More FC means more light.
learn.part.lightMeter.try: Measure the light at different times of day.
learn.part.lightMeter.numbers: Full sun: about {fc} FC. Under a cloud: about {cloudFc} FC.
learn.part.multimeter.name: Multimeter
learn.part.multimeter.how: Touch its two probes to the + and − sides. It shows the volts (V). It can also show the amps (A).
learn.part.multimeter.numbers: One panel: about {v} V. Two panels in series: about {v2} V.
learn.part.tachometer.name: Tachometer
learn.part.tachometer.what: A tachometer measures how fast something spins.
learn.part.tachometer.how: Point it at the fan. It counts how many turns the fan makes in one minute. That is RPM.
learn.part.tachometer.try: Measure the fan's speed at different times of day.
learn.part.tachometer.numbers: The fan at {v} V: about {rpm} RPM.

learn.mon.logEmpty: Press Run the day. A reading is saved every hour.

learn.m.m1.title: Build a closed-loop circuit
learn.m.m1.step.0: Pick the fan or the LED.
learn.m.m1.step.1: Tap the panel's + dot, then the device's + dot, to add a red wire.
learn.m.m1.step.2: Join the − dots to close the loop.
learn.m.m1.step.3: Turn on the sun. Does it work?
learn.m.m1.info: Electricity is the flow of electrons through a closed circuit: a complete, unbroken pathway. A solar panel has two terminals, + and −. A red wire usually means +, and a black wire means −.
learn.m.m2.title: Build a powerful system
learn.m.m2.goal: Create the most powerful system possible.
learn.m.m2.step.2: Add a cloud, then take it away.
learn.m.m2.step.3: Watch the fan. Which setting makes the most power?
learn.m.m2.info: Sketch your most powerful system. Include the sun and anything around it that you think changes how much electricity you make. Label the parts and how they affect each other.
learn.m.m3.title: Measure variables
learn.m.m3.goal: Measure the amount of light and the amount of power, first with your senses, then with tools.
learn.m.m3.step.0: Look at the light and the fan. Rate them.
learn.m.m3.step.1: Use the tools: tap a tool, then tap the panel or the fan.
learn.m.m3.step.2: Save 3 readings at different times or angles.
learn.m.m3.infoTitle: Scientific tools help us make more accurate and precise measurements
learn.m.m3.info: Solar cells turn light energy (not heat) from the sun into electricity. A light meter measures light in foot-candles (FC). A multimeter measures the voltage the panel makes. A tachometer measures the work being done: how many times the motor turns each minute (RPM).
learn.m.m4.title: Control the power
learn.m.m4.goal: Stop and start your system with a switch, and control its power with a potentiometer.
learn.m.m4.step.0: Turn the switch off and on.
learn.m.m4.step.1: Turn the dial to make the fan go slow, then fast.
learn.m.m4.step.3: Answer: does polarity make a difference?
learn.m.m4.infoTitle: How can you control the power?
learn.m.m4.info: Add a switch to turn the system on and off. Add a potentiometer (a dial) to control how much power reaches the device. Dial in the fan's speed.
learn.m.m4.info2: Energy flows out of the + side of the panel (red wire), into the + side of the device, and back to the − side. Try switching the fan's polarity: what happens? An LED's longer leg is its + side.
learn.m.m5.title: Find the limits of your system
learn.m.m5.goal: Find out which items one panel can power by itself and at the same time.
learn.m.m5.step.0: Connect one item at a time. Did it run?
learn.m.m5.step.1: Connect two or three items together.
learn.m.m5.step.2: Look at your map: a circle means it ran by itself; a line means they ran together.
learn.m.m6.title: Build a MORE powerful system
learn.m.m6.goal: Find out what you can power with TWO solar panels.
learn.m.m6.step.1: Try connecting the panels in different ways.
learn.m.m6.step.2: Find something that runs now but did not run with one panel.
learn.m.m6.info: Sketch your new system. Label HOW your panels are connected to each other and to the devices. Show polarity (+ and −).
learn.m.m7.title: Compare parallel and series circuits
learn.m.m7.goal: Work out the volts, amps and watts of two panels in series and in parallel.
learn.m.m7.step.0: Connect the panels in series. Save the reading.
learn.m.m7.step.1: Connect them in parallel. Save the reading.
learn.m.m7.step.2: Compare: what stays the same? Which way spins the fan faster?
learn.m.m7.info: Electrical power is the product of voltage and current. Voltage (V) is the push on electrons: more volts, a stronger push. Current (A) is how many electrons move past a point each second. Power = Voltage × Current.
learn.m.m7.info2: How you connect the panels doesn't change the total power, but it still matters. Work out the volts, amps and watts of each system. Series adds the voltages. Parallel adds the currents.
